vocab.definition: dissolved in water — water ions are also present.
hydrogen forms unless the metal is less reactive than H.
oxygen forms unless a halide ion is present.
shows electrons gained or lost at an electrode.

misconceptions.wrong: The metal always forms at the cathode.
misconceptions.right: Only if the metal is less reactive than hydrogen.

misconceptions.wrong: Oxygen always forms at the anode.
misconceptions.right: A halide (Cl⁻, Br⁻) forms the halogen instead.
Water provides H⁺ and OH⁻ ions too.

questions.text: Sodium chloride solution is electrolysed. Name the product at the cathode. [1 mark]
Explain why hydrogen, not sodium, forms at the cathode. [2 marks]
Name the product at the anode for sodium chloride solution. [1 mark]
Copper sulfate solution is electrolysed. Predict the products and explain why. [3 marks]
Complete the sentence using the word bank. [2 marks]
questions.secondaryText: At the cathode you get ______ unless the metal is less reactive than it; a halide gives a ______ at the anode.

questions.text: Write the half equation for hydrogen forming at the cathode. [2 marks]

footer.tip: Cathode: metal only if below hydrogen, else H₂. Anode: halogen if present, else O₂.
footer.thinkPrompt: Why does the choice of product depend on the reactivity of the ions?
